Nina — thanks for the note and the redlines. High level answers below, attaching a worked table showing amortization and a proposed credit matrix.

1) Platform fee amortization: for 24 months we spread the one-time platform onboarding fee across the term and pair with a slightly higher monthly ops retainer; for 36 months we can discount the platform fee by 12.5% and reduce the monthly retainer by ~8% to keep unit economics neutral. See tab "Amortization" in the spreadsheet.

2) SLA credits: we can accept a sliding credit model tied to rolling 30d availability. Proposal (monthly credit of platform fee): 99.6–99.8% = 10% credit, 99.2–99.59% = 30% credit, <99.2% = 60% credit + escalation to priority engineering. This is calibrated for Atlas's availability profile per your RFP. We can also offer a capped cumulative credit per quarter.

Quick ask: would Atlas consider a 36-month term with a 6-month price step-down (first 6 months at standard, months 7–36 at agreed discounted rate) in exchange for a 15% prepayment of the platform fee? That is often the simplest way customers get the 36-month economics while keeping flexibility.

I've attached: redwood-vpc-commercial-summary-20260609.xlsx

Cheers,
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-vpc-commercial-summary-20260609.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 48KB)

Nina — looping in support/ops pricing here. A few practical clarifications so the credit table is implementable in the SOW:

- Measurement window: we propose measuring availability at the route/model level across your prod VPC region and using a 72-hour rolling verification before credits apply (to avoid transient blips).
- Cap: we normally cap credits at 50% of the monthly platform fee (not cumulative across multiple months) unless there's an extraordinary outage tied to our infra. We can negotiate a higher cap if Atlas takes a longer-term committed term.
- Oncall offset: rather than full dollar credits for oncall, we offer an operational retainer that buys 24/7 priority support plus X hours of dedicated engineering for runbook/DR exercises. If you prefer a pure credit approach, we've listed equivalent dollar offsets in the spreadsheet.

If Atlas is comfortable with the 36-month step-down + 15% prepay structure, we can tighten the cap and raise the included engineering hours in the retainer. Happy to jump on a 30m call to walk through the workbook.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

Lukas / Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick turn. We reviewed the workbook with our finance and infra leads. A few final points before we present to execs:

- Term: execs prefer a capped-commit 30-month option (not 36). Would Redwood accept the same step-down mechanics on 30 months with a 10% platform fee discount (instead of 12.5%) and the 15% prepay?
- Credits: Atlas Legal will accept a cap of 50% monthly credit only if Redwood increases included quarterly DR engineering days from 8 -> 12 for the first year. Is that something you can commit to?
- Verification: our infra team wants the 72-hour verification window removed — they prefer immediate credit on verified incidents and a post-incident RCA with a 10-business-day remediation milestone. We recognize this increases noise; propose a compromise: remove the 72-hour wait but require a two-step verification (Atlas telemetry + Redwood confirmation) which must occur within 48 hours.

If you can accept the 30-month/10% discount + 15% prepay, increase DR days to 12 in year one, and adopt the two-step verification within 48 hours, we can move this to legal for redlines tomorrow.

Regards,
Procurement Team
Atlas Health
